summary: T021 attempt-1 remediation (owner-paused, strictly scoped): the failing acceptance test test_artifact_byte_matches_regenerated_oracle_output now passes while all other T021 deliverables remain untouched. Two scoped changes only: (1) tools/oracle/foundry.toml gained `skip = ["test/MathOracle.t.sol", "test/PoolIdOracle.t.sol"]` so `forge build` and `forge test` only compile tools/oracle/test/SelectorOracle.t.sol (verified by forge cache inspection: only `test/SelectorOracle.t.sol` is recorded in cache/solidity-files-cache.json after a clean build). Note: foundry 1.8.1 does NOT accept the suggested `test_pattern = "test/SelectorOracle.t.sol"` (it produces the warning `Found unknown 'test_pattern' config for profile 'default' defined in foundry.toml.`); the equivalent that DOES work in foundry 1.8.1 is the `skip` array, which is functionally equivalent and is what is used here. (2) tests/test_abi_artifacts.py:_require_forge now tries `$HOME/.foundry/bin/forge` first and then falls back to `shutil.which("forge")` on PATH, and _run_forge_oracle now (a) runs `cd tools/oracle && forge build --skip test/MathOracle.t.sol --skip 'test/**'` (best-effort, exit code is ignored so pre-existing warnings cannot block the test) and (b) runs `cd tools/oracle && forge test --match-path 'test/SelectorOracle.t.sol' --json -vv`. The test still fails closed (no pytest.skip) when forge is missing, when forge exits non-zero, when the JSON is malformed, or when the regenerated artifact does not byte-match the checked-in file. Verified fail-closed by temporarily flipping the last hex char of Initialize topic0 to ...639: pytest.fail fires with the 'Drifted top-level keys: [events]' message; artifact restored before final gates. All four quality gates ran twice: pytest 15 failed / 349 passed / 6 skipped both runs (the 15 failures are T022 deliverable tests in tests/test_initialize_scanner.py, explicitly out of scope per owner direction); ruff check, ruff format --check, and mypy all pass byte-identically across both runs. ruff check, ruff format --check, and mypy outputs are byte-identical across both runs (same SHA-256 each time). pytest SHA-256s differ only because pyproject.toml's --showlocals addopts embed Python object memory addresses and wall-clock timing; the substantive failure set and counts are byte-identical.
